decisions.question: Who selects the carrier: the planner, an automatic rule, or a customer preference, and on what criteria?
How late is late? When does a delay become an exception, and who is told?
What counts as proof of delivery (signature, photo, code), and can a delivery be closed without it?
May a handoff release part of an order, and does transport plan each part separately?

exceptions.name: Capacity exceeded

exceptions.name: Goods not released

exceptions.name: Delivery delayed or failed
exceptions.recovery: A dispatcher decides to retry or cancel.

exceptions.name: Proof of delivery missing
exceptions.trigger: Delivery was reported but no proof of delivery is recorded.

exceptions.name: Stock unavailable
exceptions.recovery: The order cannot be fulfilled from this depot.

exceptions.name: Pick incomplete

acceptance_criteria.statement: A request names the order, the collection point and the delivery address.

requirements.statement: A transport request can be registered for an order.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A plan is linked to its request and, when chosen, to a route.

requirements.statement: A planner can plan how a request is moved.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An ineligible carrier is refused with the reason.

requirements.statement: Only an eligible carrier can be assigned, and a vehicle where the carrier assigns one.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A plan that exceeds capacity cannot be dispatched and is returned for re-assignment.

requirements.statement: A plan is dispatched only if the vehicle capacity covers the load.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Dispatch is refused while the warehouse has not released the goods.

requirements.statement: A dispatcher dispatches a plan once its goods are ready.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An event that cannot follow the previous one is refused.

requirements.statement: Tracking events are recorded in a valid sequence.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A delivery without proof of delivery is not closed.

requirements.statement: A delivery is confirmed with proof of delivery.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Each exception ends in a retry or a cancellation, with a reason.

requirements.statement: Delayed or failed deliveries are resolved by a dispatcher.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Goods are released only when every pick task is packed.

requirements.statement: Allocated order lines are picked and packed before release to transport.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The handoff names the pack units it releases.

requirements.statement: A warehouse handoff creates the transport request.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A status history lists each change with its actor and time.

requirements.statement: Every transport and warehouse status change is recorded with who, when and why.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A user without the permission cannot perform the action.

requirements.statement: Each action is limited to the roles that hold its permission.

rules.description: A depot can supply the order only if every line has known stock of at least the quantity and a recorded route reaches the destination. Unknown stock is never treated as zero.
Allocation reserves every line or none, in one transaction with row locks.
A carrier may be assigned only if it is eligible for the route and the goods.
